name: FM radio broadcast
plain_meaning: Commercial FM radio stations.
check_next: Compare with the FCC list of local FM stations.

name: Aircraft voice radio
plain_meaning: Pilots and air traffic control talking. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Check for nearby airports in the site profile.

name: 2 m amateur (ham) band
plain_meaning: Licensed ham radio operators.
check_next: Look up the mode in Artemis-DB (sigidwiki) by width and modulation.

name: NOAA Weather Radio
plain_meaning: Government weather broadcasts.
check_next: Compare with the NOAA Weather Radio transmitter list.

name: 315 MHz short-range devices
plain_meaning: Car key fobs, tire pressure sensors and garage remotes.
check_next: Decode a recording with rtl_433 ({rtl433_count} device types listed in ism_devices.csv).

name: 433 MHz short-range devices
plain_meaning: Weather stations, temperature sensors, doorbells and remotes.
check_next: Decode a recording with rtl_433 ({rtl433_count} device types listed in ism_devices.csv).

name: 868 MHz short-range devices (Europe)
plain_meaning: European band for sensors, alarms and LoRa. Rare in the US.
check_next: Decode with rtl_433; if the site is in the US ask why a European device is here.

name: Cellular low band
plain_meaning: Phone network (4G/5G) towers and phones.
check_next: Check for cell towers in the site profile.

name: 902-928 MHz ISM band
plain_meaning: Utility meters, LoRa sensors and other unlicensed devices.
check_next: Decode with rtl_433; LoRa needs a LoRa decoder.

name: Long-range drone control (900 MHz)
plain_meaning: Hobby and long-range drone remote-control links hop around this band.
check_next: Listen for Remote ID; compare the hop pattern with known drone radios.
source: FCC Part 15.247; drone radio specs (to verify)

name: Aircraft distance measuring (DME/TACAN)
plain_meaning: Aircraft and ground beacons measuring distance. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Check for nearby airports in the site profile.

name: Ground radar questions to aircraft (1030 MHz)
plain_meaning: Airport radar asking aircraft transponders to reply. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Check for nearby airports in the site profile.

name: Aircraft transponder replies (ADS-B / Mode S)
plain_meaning: Aircraft broadcasting their position. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Decode with an ADS-B decoder (dump1090) to see the aircraft.
source: NTIA US Frequency Allocation Chart; OpenSky Network

name: Long-range air surveillance radar
plain_meaning: Air route and military surveillance radar. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Check FAA radar sites near the area.

name: GPS / GNSS L1
plain_meaning: Satellite navigation. Real satellite signals sit below the noise, so any signal strong enough to be seen here may be interference or jamming.
check_next: Check whether nearby GPS receivers lose their fix; compare with GPSJam or OpenSky navigation-accuracy reports for the area.
source: NTIA US Frequency Allocation Chart; GPSJam; OpenSky Network

name: Cellular mid band
plain_meaning: Phone network (4G/5G) towers and phones.
check_next: Check for cell towers in the site profile.

name: Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz
plain_meaning: Wireless internet routers and devices.
check_next: Normal almost everywhere people are.

name: Bluetooth
plain_meaning: Phones, headphones and other Bluetooth devices.
check_next: Normal almost everywhere people are.

name: Drone control link (2.4 GHz)
plain_meaning: Drone remote-control links hop around this band.
check_next: Listen for Remote ID on Bluetooth (2402, 2426, 2480 MHz) and Wi-Fi; compare with DroneDetect and CardRF recordings.

name: Drone video link (2.4 GHz)
plain_meaning: Drone video downlinks; they look a lot like Wi-Fi.
check_next: Listen for Remote ID; check whether the signal hops between channels the way Wi-Fi does not.

name: Cellular 2.5 GHz
plain_meaning: Phone network (4G/5G).
check_next: Check for cell towers in the site profile.

name: Airport and weather radar (S band)
plain_meaning: Airport surveillance and NEXRAD weather radar. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Check for nearby airports and NEXRAD sites in the site profile.

name: Military radar (3.1-3.45 GHz)
plain_meaning: Military land and ship radar. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Check for military installations near the area.

name: 3.45 GHz 5G (shared with military radar)
plain_meaning: Phone network (5G) in a band shared with military radar.
check_next: Check for cell towers in the site profile.

name: Navy radar in the CBRS band
plain_meaning: Shipborne and coastal Navy radar, which CBRS networks must give way to. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Inland it is unusual; check for military activity or test ranges nearby.
source: NTIA US Frequency Allocation Chart; NIST 3.5 GHz radar dataset

name: CBRS shared band
plain_meaning: Private LTE/5G networks that must give way to Navy radar.
check_next: Check whether a private network is licensed near the site.

name: 5G C-band
plain_meaning: Phone network (5G).
check_next: Check for cell towers in the site profile.

name: Aircraft radar altimeters
plain_meaning: Aircraft measuring their height above ground. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Expect only while aircraft are low overhead.

name: Wi-Fi 5 GHz
plain_meaning: Wireless internet routers and devices.
check_next: Normal almost everywhere people are.

name: Terminal Doppler weather radar (C band)
plain_meaning: Weather radar at large airports. Safety of life: listen only.
check_next: Check for a TDWR site near the area.

name: Drone video link (5.8 GHz)
plain_meaning: Drone and FPV video downlinks.
check_next: Listen for Remote ID; analog FM video in this band is almost always FPV.
source: FCC Part 15.247; drone radio specs (to verify)

name: Drone control link (5.8 GHz)
plain_meaning: Drone remote-control links hop around this band.
check_next: Listen for Remote ID; compare with known drone radios.
source: FCC Part 15.247; drone radio specs (to verify)
